source_text: Τοιοῦτος ὁ περὶ τὸ θεῖον ἀληθὴς λόγος, ὦ ἄνθρωποι Ἕλληνές τε καὶ βάρβαροι, Χαλδαῖοί τε καὶ Ἀσσύριοι, Αἰγύπτιοί τε καὶ Λίβυες, Ἰνδοί τε καὶ Αἰθίοπες, Κελτοί τε καὶ οἱ στρατηγοῦντες Λατῖνοι, πάντες τε οἱ τὴν Εὐρώπην Ἀσίαν τε καὶ Λιβύην κατοικοῦντες, οἷς σύμβουλος ἐγὼ γίνομαι, φιλανθρώπου λόγου ὑπάρχων μαθητὴς καὶ φιλάνθρωπος, ὅπως προσδραμόντες διδαχθῆτε παρ᾿ ἡμῶν, τίς ὁ ὄντως θεὸς καὶ ἡ τούτου εὔτακτος δημιουργία, μὴ προσέχοντες σοφίσμασιν ἐντέχνων λόγων, μηδὲ ματαίοις ἐπαγγελίαις κλεψιλόγων αἱρετικῶν, ἀλλ᾿ ἀληθείας ἀκόμπου ἁπλότητι σεμνῇ, δι᾿ ἧς ἐπιγνώσεως ἐκφεύξεσθε ἐπερχομένην πυρὸς κρίσεως ἀπειλὴν καὶ ταρτάρου ζοφεροῦ ὄμμα ἀφώτιστον, ὑπὸ λόγου φωνῆς μὴ καταλαμφθέν, καὶ βρασμὸν ἀεννάου λίμνης γεέννης φλογός, καὶ ταρταρούχων ἀγγέλων κολαστῶν ὄμμα ἀεὶ μένον ἐν ἀπειλῇ, καὶ σκώληκα σώματος ἀπουσίαν ἐπιστρεφόμενον, ἐπὶ τὸ ἐκβράσαν σῶμα ὡς ἐπιστρέφων.
pass_a_gloss: Such is the true discourse concerning the divine, oh men, Greeks and barbarians, Chaldeans and Assyrians, Egyptians and Libyans, Indians and Ethiopians, Celts and the Latin commanders, and all those inhabiting Europe and Asia and Libya, to whom I become an advisor, being a student of philanthropic discourse and philanthropic, so that having run to us you may be taught what the truly existing God is and the well-ordered creation of this one, not paying attention to the cleverness of cunning words, nor to the vain promises of heretical thieves of words, but with the noble simplicity of unadulterated truth, through which knowledge you will escape the impending threat of the fire of judgment and the gloomy eye of Tartarus unextinguished, not being seized by the voice of the word, and the burning of the eternal lake of Gehenna's fire, and the eye of the angels of Tartarus who punish always remaining in threat, and the worm of the body's absence returning, upon the body as it returns after being burned

pass_b_english: Such is the true discourse concerning the divine, O men—Greeks and barbarians, Chaldeans and Assyrians, Egyptians and Libyans, Indians and Ethiopians, Celts and the Latin commanders, and all who inhabit Europe, Asia, and Libya. To all of you I offer myself as an advisor, since I am a student of philanthropic discourse and philanthropic myself. My purpose is that you may come running to us and be taught who the truly existing God is and what his well-ordered creation is like. Do not pay attention to the cleverness of cunning words or to the empty promises of heretical word-thieves. Instead, embrace the noble simplicity of unadulterated truth. Through the knowledge it brings you will escape the impending threat of the fire of judgment, the gloomy, unextinguished eye of Tartarus, the burning of the eternal lake of Gehenna’s fire, and the ever-watchful, threatening eye of the angels of Tartarus who punish. You will also escape the worm that returns upon the resurrected body after it has been burned, feeding on it once more as it turns back to it.

review.notes: Pass B adds significant theological interpretation and content not present in the Greek source, specifically regarding the 'worm' and the 'resurrected body'. The Greek text describes the worm as 'returning to the body that has been burned' (σκώληκα σώματος ἀπουσίαν ἐπιστρεφόμενον, ἐπὶ τὸ ἐκβράσαν σῶμα ὡς ἐπιστρέφων), whereas Pass B adds 'resurrected body' and 'feeding on it once more', which are not in the source text.
reasons: Pass B adds content not found in the Greek: 'resurrected body' and 'feeding on it once more' in relation to the worm (σκώληκα σώματος ἀπουσίαν ἐπιστρεφόμενον, ἐπὶ τὸ ἐκβράσαν σῶμα ὡς ἐπιστρέφων).
